import pandas as pd

def main():
    # Define source file paths
    source_files = [
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_49/test_0.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_49/test_1.csv"
    ]

    # Define the target schema columns and their types
    target_columns = [
        'tripduration', 'starttime', 'stoptime', 'start station id', 'start station name',
        'start station latitude', 'start station longitude', 'end station id', 'end station name',
        'end station latitude', 'end station longitude', 'bikeid', 'usertype', 'birth year', 'gender'
    ]

    # Data types for enforcing target schema
    dtype_map = {
        'tripduration': 'int64',
        'starttime': 'string',
        'stoptime': 'string',
        'start station id': 'Int64',  # Nullable integer
        'start station name': 'string',
        'start station latitude': 'float64',
        'start station longitude': 'float64',
        'end station id': 'Int64',
        'end station name': 'string',
        'end station latitude': 'float64',
        'end station longitude': 'float64',
        'bikeid': 'Int64',
        'usertype': 'string',
        'birth year': 'Int64',
        'gender': 'Int64'
    }

    # Load all source dataframes into a list
    dfs = []
    for file_path in source_files:
        df = pd.read_csv(file_path, dtype=str)  # Read all as string first to avoid dtype issues
        dfs.append(df)

    # Concatenate all source dataframes vertically (union)
    combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

    # Convert columns to target dtypes carefully
    # For numeric columns, convert with errors='coerce' to handle any bad data gracefully
    numeric_columns = [
        'tripduration', 'start station id', 'start station latitude', 'start station longitude',
        'end station id', 'end station latitude', 'end station longitude', 'bikeid', 'birth year', 'gender'
    ]
    for col in numeric_columns:
        if col in combined_df.columns:
            combined_df[col] = pd.to_numeric(combined_df[col], errors='coerce')

    # For string columns, ensure type string and strip whitespace
    string_columns = ['starttime', 'stoptime', 'start station name', 'end station name', 'usertype']
    for col in string_columns:
        if col in combined_df.columns:
            combined_df[col] = combined_df[col].astype(str).str.strip()

    # Enforce the target schema column order and presence
    # If any target column is missing, create it with NaNs
    for col in target_columns:
        if col not in combined_df.columns:
            combined_df[col] = pd.NA

    combined_df = combined_df[target_columns]

    # Convert dtypes again to enforce target schema precisely
    for col, dtype in dtype_map.items():
        if dtype == 'string':
            combined_df[col] = combined_df[col].astype('string')
        elif dtype == 'Int64':
            combined_df[col] = combined_df[col].astype('Int64')
        else:
            combined_df[col] = combined_df[col].astype(dtype)

    # Save the combined dataframe to the target path as CSV
    target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_49/target_multisource_cot.csv"
    combined_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
